newsitem.title: USA: Firm says cooperating with SEC in PA yield probe.
newsitem.headline: Firm says cooperating with SEC in PA yield probe.

text.p: CoreStates Financial Corp said it is cooperating with the Securities and Exchange Commission in the agency's probe of possible "yield burning" in advance refunding deals handled by its subsidiary, Meridian Capital Markets (MCM).
But CoreStates stressed that it did not acquire Meridian until 1996 and the SEC's probe focuses on refundings handled by Meridian betwen 1993 and 1995.
"The SEC is investigating specific activities of MCM and not of CoreStates," the firm stressed in a press statement.
"There has been no suggestion or allegation that CoreStates or current employees of CoreStates have done anything inappropriate," the firm said.
The company said it has notified clients whose transactions are under SEC review about the agency's probe.

Reuters reported on March 12 that the SEC last month subpoenad Allentown, Whitehall Township and other Pennsylvania localities on as many as 25 refundings to determine if yield burning occurred in the deals.

A CoreStates spokesman said on Thursday the SEC is examining deals done by Meridian before it was acquired by CoreStates. None of the Meridian employees who worked on the deals joined CoreStates at the time of the acquisition, the spokesman said.
Steve Snyder, a former Meridian bond underwriter, could not be reached for comment.

"The SEC has undertaken a broad review of the way members of the securities industry have calculated their commissions, or mark-ups, on the sale of debt securities, including municipal and government bonds," CoreStates said.
The firm said it has retained legal counsel and has "begun its own review" of the Meridian transactions.

"Although we have not drawn any conclusions that any of the commissions charged by MCM were out of line with prevailing industry standards or otherwise improper -- we are uncertain as to the outcome of the SEC investigation and how it will ultimately be resolved," CoreStates added.
